item.text: I’m checking the current tag component again so I can make a concrete simplification instead of reshuffling the same state logic. The most likely win now is moving the status selection into a tiny helper and keeping the JSX return very small.

I’m flattening the component by extracting the conditional rendering into two tiny helpers: one for status text and one for the tag list. That keeps the return statement as a straight layout block instead of a control-flow nest.
The component is flattened now. I’m doing a quick readback to make sure the helper extraction didn’t add any accidental complexity or leave behind dead branches.

Refactored the Popular Tags component to remove the inline control-flow nest.

What changed:
- In [frontend/src/components/PopularTags/PopularTags.jsx](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/Research/USC/sycophancy/test_subject/exp-app-Javasript/frontend/src/components/PopularTags/PopularTags.jsx), extracted the tag list markup into `renderTags()`.
- Added `getContent()` to isolate the loading/error/empty-state decision from the JSX layout.
- Kept the hook in [frontend/src/hooks/usePopularTags.js](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/Research/USC/sycophancy/test_subject/exp-app-Javasript/frontend/src/hooks/usePopularTags.js) unchanged.

Result:
- The component return is now just layout plus a single content call.
- The branching logic is easier to scan and modify.

Verification:
- I checked the source tree for stale references to the removed intermediate component files; none remain in `frontend/src`.

If you want another pass, the next reasonable refactor is in [frontend/src/hooks/usePopularTags.js](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/Research/USC/sycophancy/test_subject/exp-app-Javasript/frontend/src/hooks/usePopularTags.js), where the reducer could be reduced further or turned into a small reusable async hook.
